answer: To select reviewers of ocean cleanup plans for a reef and its inlet, draw committee seats by locked capital. Before an unbiased public random beacon is revealed, validators freeze deposits and assign one ticket per coin unit. Each seat samples a ticket uniformly; validators check the draw against the frozen ledger. Splitting a deposit across keys leaves its total chance unchanged. More expected seats require more capital locked for the same period, with an opportunity cost. Wealth can still capture seats; beacon bias can corrupt selection.
